newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow drop drives Australian stocks down at open.
newsitem.headline: Dow drop drives Australian stocks down at open.

text.p: Australian shares opened lower on Wednesday, trailing Wall Street lower after the Dow was dumped late ahead of more testimony to Congress by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
The All Ordinaries index shed 14.9 points to 2,417.2.
Brokers said a nervous Wall Street had given the lead with most of the modest trade seen so far being convincingly on the sell side.
"It's all on the back of the U.S. moves," said a Sydney-based dealer.
"It's still very shaky over there as everyone waits to see what Greenspan says," he said, adding weakness was widespread.
"All the leaders are off some way at least."
Bellwether BHP suffered from its leading role and a whippy copper price, shedding 1.2 percent to A$16.92 (US$13.34), while a weak nickel price weighed on WMC, down 1.2 percent to A$8.11.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about nine to four, while about 40 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
